expected_discriminating_result: The phase-transition comparison should change the resolved radial thermal trajectory and at least one declared surface or integrated observable relative to the standard-cooling comparison under the same initial state.
falsification_condition: The PDE solution fails numerical verification, violates declared field or boundary bounds, or produces no distinguishable observable across comparison scenarios within the declared model domain.
hypothesis_delta: A spatially resolved neutron-star thermal evolution model will produce pathway-specific radial temperature and surface-emission signatures that are not identifiable from the lumped ODE alone.
model_delta: Replace the lumped thermal state with an executable spatially resolved PDE model selected from the approved PDE capability catalog.
Require the model contract to declare spatial domain, field, initial condition, boundary conditions, parameters, observables, comparison scenarios, numerical method, and falsification conditions.
Use a fixed trusted PDE adapter only; do not generate or execute free-form source code.
Preserve the parent Q2 mechanism-replacement lineage and make the PDE result usable by the standalone quantitative report and Author handoff.
parameter_or_boundary_delta: Introduce the spatial and temporal resolution and the thermal transport/source/boundary quantities required by the selected PDE family.
Bind every new numeric parameter to an explicit evidence or model-assumption status before execution.
revision_reason: The qualified lumped ODE baseline does not resolve spatial thermal transport inside the neutron star. Upgrade this branch to an executable spatially resolved PDE so the model can test whether phase-transition and cooling signatures are distinguishable across the stellar interior while retaining the existing pulsar-evolution comparison context.
